items.title: Fahmi: Prasarana to operate 24-hour services for National Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: This year's National Day celebration will see Prasarana operate public transport services around the clock on the night of Aug 30 leading into Aug 31, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. "Prasarana has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with National Day. Fahmi was speaking to reporters after officiating at Majlis Ekspresi Jalur Gemilang JAPEN@Petronas at Petronas NPE Pantai Dalam here.

items.title: Bangladeshi man held after housemate slashed over misunderstandings
items.summary: The suspect, 30, is also a colleague of the victim, a 36-year-old Bangladeshi man. Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect was arrested in front of a polyclinic in Kampung Cheras Baru. Rosdi said the victim, who works as a store assistant, was in stable condition at Ampang Hospital.

items.title: Three freed after fallen tree traps them inside car in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Three people were rescued after a tree fell on the Perodua Ativa they were travelling in along Jalan Macalister this morning. The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 9.12am and dispatched eight firefighters from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene. “All three victims who were trapped inside the vehicle were successfully freed by members of the public before the rescue team arrived,” the department said.

items.title: Afghanistan's gold rush upends lives and landscapes
items.summary: AFGHANISTAN: In Afghanistan's northeastern Badakhshan province, dozens of excavators operate day and night to extract gold from the mountains where villagers and their livestock once roamed. Thousands of miners are deployed across the Shiwa area, about 50 kilometres (30 miles) northeast of the provincial capital Faizabad, extracting gold for investors nationwide. "Before, the river was deep, the water was clean," said the 74-year-old from Pul-e-Ziri Ban valley.

items.title: Angklung tunes along Sarawak River strengthen Malaysia Indonesia ties
items.summary: The music symbolised the close friendship between Malaysia and Indonesia through cultural diplomacy as both countries celebrate their independence month. The programme also provided wider opportunities for cultural exchange and strengthened relations between the people of both countries. "We are holding a cultural arts goodwill event to introduce and promote Indonesian cultural arts, especially angklung, dance, batik and kebaya to the community in Sarawak in conjunction with the celebration of the Republic of Indonesia's Independence Day.

items.title: Rauf: Elected representatives must understand people's hardships
items.summary: MELAKA: Elected representatives in the state have been reminded to remain mindful of the hardships faced by the people, including during floods, and not regard their positions as a privilege. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said those holding elected office had a responsibility to serve all people regardless of race, religion, background or political ideology. Rauf said his concern for the people's well-being during bad weather had also led him to constantly monitor the possibility of floods or other untoward incidents.

items.title: Malaysia awaits US response on excess capacity after concluding forced-labour tariff talks, says Johari Ghani
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 9 — Malaysia is awaiting Washington’s response on concerns over industrial excess capacity after completing the forced-labour component of its discussions with the US, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. The Star reported that Johari, speaking at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia’s (ACCCIM) 80th annual general meeting here, said the government would continue engaging the US on the outstanding issue. Under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, Malaysia has committed to prohibit imports made using forced labour as well as take steps to address global excess capacity in the steel sector.

items.title: Fijian foreign and external trade minister visits Malaysia to strengthen ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fijian Foreign and External Trade Minister, Sakiasi Raisevu Ditoka, will undertake a working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to Wednesday to further strengthen bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Fiji. Malaysia's Foreign Ministry in a statement said during the visit, Ditoka will meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss efforts to further strengthen bilateral cooperation between the two countries, particularly in trade and investment, capacity building, forestry, renewable energy, and culture. In 2025, total bilateral trade between Malaysia and Fiji amounted to RM880.01 million (US$206.2 million), with Malaysia's exports valued at RM867.92 million (US$203.41 million) and imports from Fiji valued at RM12.09 million (US$2.80 million).

items.title: Johari: Malaysia must not open market faster than local industries can adapt
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Malaysia must avoid opening its market to foreign competition faster than domestic industries can adapt, particularly when local companies are up against much larger players with significant economies of scale. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said foreign investment should complement local industries by bringing in technology and capabilities Malaysia lacks, rather than displacing businesses built up over decades. Citing the iron and steel industry, Johari said Malaysia had developed it over decades, but local players subsequently struggled after the market was opened to much larger foreign producers with significantly greater production capacity.

items.title: EC to prepare updated report on Sarawak bid for 17 new seats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Election Commission (EC) to prepare an updated report on Sarawak's proposal to add 17 new state assembly seats, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. Ministers Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi raised the matter at a recent cabinet meeting, he said. "The prime minister's commitment is to implement it," he said.

items.title: CAP urges crackdown on motorists vaping behind the wheel
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Road users could face growing risks from motorists vaping while driving unless the government takes decisive action to curb the practice, says the Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP). Its education officer N.V. Subbarow said the association had received numerous complaints about motorists, including express bus and lorry drivers and motorcyclists, vaping on the road. Subbarow called for strict enforcement against motorists caught vaping or using drug-laced vape products while driving, including hefty compounds and, for serious or repeat offences, suspension or disqualification of driving licences.

items.title: 2 Mercedes-Benz seized after businessmen 'forget' road tax, insurance
items.summary: KLANG: Two businessmen had their Mercedes-Benz cars seized by the Road Transport Department (RTD) after the luxury vehicles were found to have no valid road tax or insurance coverage. Selangor RTD director Datuk Ahmad Kamarunzaman Mehat said both men were stopped during Ops Luxury at Taman Berkeley and the Federal Highway. Checks found that the licences for both cars had expired around May and that the vehicles had no valid insurance.

items.title: Asean at 59: Bolstering centrality from within as bloc advances Vision 2045
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (Asean) marked its 59th anniversary yesterday, the bloc finds itself at a pivotal time as it navigates new geopolitical realities reshaping the region. Rather, analysts said for the 11-member association, strengthening internal unity and regional integration is now more crucial than ever as both will be key to preserving ASEAN's centrality and resilience amid rising geopolitical competition and complex regional challenges. "Ideally, Asean member states themselves have to insist on it, that Asean is always a central and pivotal actor as a grouping.

items.title: Myanmar refugee figures soon, Saifuddin Nasution vows biometric drive for repatriation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — Preliminary data on Myanmar refugees who are currently identified through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme is expected to be obtained in the fourth quarter of this year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Home Ministry (KDN) through the Immigration Department (JIM) is implementing the data collection process with relevant parties. “We are conducting a data collection.

items.title: Driver's failure to engage 'P' gear led to KKIA SUV crash — Police
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: An SUV is believed to have moved on its own after its driver apparently failed to engage the 'P' (park) gear before crashing through the glass doors of the Departure Hall at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) on Friday. Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said preliminary investigations found that the woman had apparently failed to engage the 'P' gear while preparing to switch drivers. Shahrudin said the woman managed to get out of the SUV before the collision but suffered minor facial injuries from shattered glass.

items.title: 76 illegal dumpsites remain active in Selangor
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor has identified 76 illegal dumpsites that remain active as the state government steps up efforts to curb illegal dumping. Selangor Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said the state government was adopting an approach covering prevention, monitoring, cleanup and enforcement. "At the same time, the state government is expanding the use of closed-circuit television cameras at illegal dumping hotspots to help with monitoring and detecting offences, alongside strengthening integrated action between local authorities, KDEB Waste Management, district land offices and related enforcement agencies," he said.

items.title: Ngeh dismisses claims DAP reps staying in govt for posts, pay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A senior DAP leader has dismissed claims that the party's representatives want to remain in government to keep the perks and salaries that come with their ministerial posts. "Ultimately, the question of whether DAP should remain in government must be decided by party members. Next week's DAP congress will see delegates decide whether the party's representatives should remain in government.

items.title: Sabah waters exploited as transit routes for cross-border drug syndicates
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Cross-border drug syndicates are exploiting Sabah's vast maritime frontier, including waters off Semporna and Tawau, as transit points to move methamphetamine and other drugs between Malaysia and neighbouring countries. Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director-general Maritime Admiral Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said the syndicates were taking advantage of hundreds of small islands, secluded jetties, long coastlines and traditional sea routes to evade detection. For large-scale smuggling operations, Rosli said syndicates used commercial vessels to evade the authorities.

items.title: Iran issues demands for reopening of Hormuz
items.summary: DUBAI: Iran set preconditions on Saturday for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including compensation for war damages, complicating a potential deal to open the waterway essential to the world economy. Iran's Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said Hormuz's reopening had "nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman", adding that the "enemy is forced to accept Iran's conditions for the opening of the strait." Oman's foreign ministry on Saturday condemned "repeated attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz", without naming Iran.

items.title: 'Wishing them a speedy recovery': Anwar visits Ismail Sabri and Fadillah at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof and former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who are both receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN), yesterday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he made the visits with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, was admitted to IJN on August 6 after experiencing health issues while having his statement recorded at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission headquarters.

items.title: Japanese cuisine to boost Japan's agricultural and seafood product exports to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Japanese cuisine, driven by demand for halal food products and rising consumer incomes, will boost exports of Japanese agricultural and seafood products to Malaysia, said Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) Kuala Lumpur managing director Koichi Takano. "Malaysia now ranks 10th among all export destinations for Japanese agricultural, forestry, fishery, and food products, improving from 13th place previously. Malaysia as a Gateway for the Expansion of Japanese Food Products Across the Asean region, he said, Malaysia has strong potential as a gateway for the expansion of Japanese food culture and products.

items.title: Pakatan hails BN openness, Fahmi says Melaka seat talks offer chance for stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) welcomes the openness of Barisan Nasional (BN) regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and describes it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined. “The chairman of Keadilan Melaka, Yang Berhormat Adam Adli, also informed that he had been in direct contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof (regarding the distribution of Melaka State Legislative Assembly seats). Fahmi, who is also the Communications Minister, said in this regard several matters could be managed at the state and federal levels regarding the distribution of state seats in Melaka.

items.title: Anwar, Wan Azizah visit Fadillah and Ismail Sabri at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof at the National Heart Institute (IJN) yesterday. Anwar said Fadillah was recovering well but still needed rest following his heart bypass surgery. During the visit, the couple also called on former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is receiving treatment and undergoing a procedure for an irregular heartbeat.

items.title: 4,000 Myanmar nationals in immigration depots to undergo refugee screening
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department and police have begun screening Myanmar nationals held at immigration depots to determine their refugee status, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said authorities had identified about 4,000 Myanmar nationals currently held at immigration depots, stressing that this did not mean all had refugee status. On Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that repatriation would proceed with certain considerations, as Malaysia would not return Myanmar refugees if their lives were at risk.

items.title: China July factory-gate inflation eases to three-month low, CPI slows
items.summary: BEIJING: China's producer price inflation eased more than expected in July to its weakest in three months, while consumer inflation also cooled, official data showed on Sunday, as global energy prices retreated despite the US-Israel war against Iran. "Lower oil prices, combined with weakening demand, caused both (consumer and producer price inflation) in July to come in below expectations. Oil price trends remain uncertain, meaning their impact on inflation is also likely to be uncertain," said Zhaopeng Xing, ANZ's senior China strategist.

items.title: 'Near collision' at Sydney Airport triggers investigation
items.summary: SYDNEY: Safety regulators launched an investigation on Sunday into a "near collision" between two passenger aircraft at Australia's busiest airport that injured a crew member. "A cabin crew member aboard the [Jetstar] A320 was injured, and there was damage to the connection between the 777 nose gear and aircraft tug" as both planes stopped abruptly, the statement said. Investigators are collecting data from both aircraft, air traffic control, and interviewing crew and tug operators to determine the cause of the near collision, the regulator said.

items.title: 1,524 wild animal attacks since 2020 leave 54 dead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) recorded 1,524 human-wildlife conflict cases between 2020 and July this year. Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the incidents resulted in 1,470 injuries and 54 fatalities. "These conditions force wildlife to seek new roaming areas near forests, plantations, and neighbouring villages.

items.title: Animal rights group urges probe into puppy death
items.summary: Animal rights group urges probe into puppy death New Straits Times KUALA LUMPUR: Police and relevant authorities have been urged to treat the death of a puppy allegedly struck twice by a vehicle as an urgent animal cruelty case and not allow it to become another routine file. Rajesh said the incident, as described in a police report lodged at the Lukut Police Station, involved the vehicle striking a white puppy before allegedly hitting it a second time, resulting in its death. Rajesh said what made the case particularly troubling was the alleged second impact involving the same animal.

items.title: Bersatu turns to RoS after Hadi says party automatically out of Perikatan
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) reportedly plans to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over claims that its Perikatan Nasional (PN) membership had automatically lapsed after the party expressed its intention to form a new political coalition. “PN is not PAS. PN must be managed in accordance with the PN constitution, fairly, transparently and with integrity, without denying the rights of its members.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution vows scanner upgrade, promises smarter baggage checks after pilot drug scandal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — The government will look into upgrading scanning machines at airports nationwide as part of efforts to strengthen security and improve the effectiveness of baggage screening, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the government was always open to exploring the use of the latest screening equipment in line with technological advancements, particularly at the country’s main entry points. Saifuddin Nasution said baggage screening at airports was the responsibility of the Aviation Security (AVSEC) team and was in line with international airport screening standards under the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).

items.title: [UPDATED] Melaka polls: PKR, BN in talks, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR is in discussions with all parties ahead of the Melaka election, including Barisan Nasional (BN), says party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had expressed openness to cross-party engagement, which PKR welcomed. "Datuk Seri Rauf, the Chief Minister, has expressed openness to discussing with any party.

items.title: Residents fume over nightly smoke from illegal dumpsite
items.summary: DENGKIL: Residents here have been enduring smoke from open burning at an illegal dumpsite almost every night since 2022, with some claiming the fumes have caused breathing difficulties and posed a health risk. "The latest incident occurred yesterday (Friday), when the area caught fire, forcing residents to contact the Fire and Rescue Department as the blaze spread to nearby areas," he said. Meanwhile, Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant state director of operations Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 3.08am on Friday.

items.title: Indonesia closes all access to Mount Bromo as wildfire expands
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia has closed Mount Bromo national park in East Java for all tourist activities, its operator said late on Saturday, as a wildfire, burning since Monday, expanded in its caldera area. * The closure took effect from Saturday evening, for an undetermined duration, the park operator said on its official Instagram page. East Java's disaster mitigation agency said authorities are deploying water bombing helicopters and water spraying drones to bolster efforts to extinguish the fire.

items.title: Marzuki slams PN for questioning Bersatu's 'moral courage'
items.summary: Datuk Dr Marzuki Mohamad said Bersatu, which Muhyiddin leads, had the right to question its position in PN in line with the coalition's constitution, which must be respected by all parties. "Bersatu was said to have automatically lost its membership in PN when it contested using its own logo and announced the formation of a new coalition in the recent Negri Sembilan election. Separately, Marzuki claimed Bersatu was barred from attending the PN Supreme Council meeting to discuss seat allocations for the Negri Sembilan state election on July 16, which he said violated the coalition's constitution.

items.title: Many members want DAP to stay in govt, says Ngeh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Many DAP members want the party to remain in government, says its national treasurer Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham ahead of next week's national congress. Ngeh, who is Beruas member of parliament, said feedback showed most members wanted DAP to stay in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration to fulfil the people's mandate. Next week's DAP congress will see delegates decide whether the party's representatives should remain in government.

items.title: 30-metre tree crashes onto car in George Town, injuring family of 3
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Three people, including a 9-year-old girl, were injured when a 30-metre Angsana tree fell onto their Perodua Ativa along Jalan Macalister this morning. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the incident, which happened around 9am, occurred in front of Tropicana 218 Macalister along the road heading towards Komtar. Francis said the victims were given initial treatment before being taken to Penang Hospital.

items.title: Immigration Dept probes vehicle bearing its logo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department is investigating the unauthorised use of its logo on a vehicle driven by a foreigner after images of the vehicle went viral on social media. Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle was neither owned by nor an official asset of the department. "An investigation is underway to identify the person involved and determine the purpose of using the department's logo on the vehicle.

items.title: Govt ends 40-year settlement issue with land grants for 120 Perak families, says housing minister
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 9 — A total of 120 squatter families around Sungkai and Kuala Bikam have been given land grants, resolving a settlement issue they had faced for more than 40 years, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. In a statement last night, Nga said the resolution of the issue was proof that the Madani Government always prioritised the wellbeing of the people regardless of racial background and social status, in line with its commitment to ensuring no Malaysian was left behind or marginalised in development. Last night, 120 families are receiving land grants that symbolise a more secure future for them and future generations,” he said.

items.title: Immigration investigates video of vehicle reportedly misusing department logo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The Immigration Department is investigating the use of its logo on a vehicle seen in a viral social media post and reportedly driven by a foreign national. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle did not belong to the department and was not one of its official assets. The department said investigations were under way to identify the individual involved and determine the purpose behind the use of its logo on the vehicle.

items.title: Perlis Umno gears up to contest all seats solo at next election
items.summary: ARAU, Aug 9 — Perlis Umno is preparing its machinery to contest all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies on its own at the next election, state liaison chairman Datuk Rozabil Abd Rahman reprotedly said. Berita Harian reported that Rozabil said there had so far been no official talks with any political party, including Perikatan Nasional (PN), on electoral cooperation in Perlis. He said the state chapter, which failed to win any seat in Perlis at the last election, would leave any eventual decision on electoral cooperation to the party’s national leadership.

items.title: Five Sarawak areas record unhealthy API levels amid transboundary haze
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Five areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am today, compared with six areas yesterday afternoon. Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings were Kuching (153), Samarahan (156), Serian (170), Bintulu (156) and Samalaju (151). Uggah, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the areas identified were Betong, Bintulu, Daro, Julau, Kanowit, Kuching, Lundu, Marudi, Miri, Mukah, Pakan, Samarahan, Saratok, Serian, Sibu, Simunjan, Song, Sri Aman and Tatau.

items.title: Police track Perodua Alza occupants after passenger seen leaning out of rear window
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Police are tracking the driver and passenger of a Perodua Alza following a viral video showing the passenger sticking part of their body out of the rear window while the vehicle was moving along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway. Kajang police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the 12-second video went viral on Threads yesterday, with the incident believed to have occurred at KM1 of the expressway towards Kajang. He urged anyone with information on the incident to contact the nearest police station or the investigating officer, Insp Afiq Rifdi Mohd Azmi, at 011-29667474.

items.title: Man drowns while attempting to rescue eight-year-old son from Raub resort fish pond
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 9 — A man drowned while trying to save his son who had fallen into a fish pond at a resort in Sungai Ruan, Raub yesterday. Raub District Police chief Supt Mohd Shahril Abdul Rahman said police received information on the incident involving Mohamed Hafidz Che Din, 46, at about 3pm. He said preliminary investigations found that the victim jumped into the pond to save his eight-year-old son, who had fallen in while trying to retrieve a plastic bread bag used as fishing bait.

items.title: Works Ministry eyes bigger Budget 2027 allocation for development and maintenance
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 9 — The Works Ministry (KKR) hopes to receive the highest development allocation among ministries in Budget 2027, to enable more development and infrastructure maintenance projects to be carried out nationwide. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said KKR was currently gathering input from agencies under the ministry, including the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia (CIDB) and Public Works Department (JKR), in preparation for Budget 2027. Meanwhile, Ahmad said KKR, through LLM, was strengthening efforts to develop smart highways through digital technology, artificial intelligence (AI), closed-circuit television (CCTV), smart lanes and the local navigation application TuJu.

items.title: Penang halts use of automatic number plate recognition for parking offences over public concerns
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — The Penang state government has instructed both local authorities in the state to immediately suspend the implementation of the Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for issuing compounds, to allow a review of its details. “The state government will instruct both local authorities, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP)) to immediately suspend the implementation of ANPR and review its details. Chow said the matter was among those discussed during a meeting with Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim and Penang DAP deputy chairman Zairil Khir Johari after he chaired the Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) Leadership Council meeting here yesterday.

items.title: Six remanded over Alor Setar kidnapping case after police rescue two foreign nationals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Six individuals arrested to assist in investigations into the abduction of two foreign nationals in Alor Setar have been placed under remand for seven days beginning yesterday. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects comprise a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, who were arrested in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur. The operation also saw the rescue of the two victims - a foreign man in his 70s and a foreign woman in her 30s - who were found blindfolded and handcuffed.

items.title: Anwar hails AKPS for seizing suspected Israel-bound shipment at Johor port
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his appreciation to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) for its swift action in seizing a container suspected of carrying strategic goods for export to Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor Friday. Anwar said Malaysia would continue to uphold the principles of humanity, justice and international law in defending the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people. Earlier, AKPS said in a statement that it had detained and inspected a container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas Friday that was suspected of carrying goods for export to Israel.

items.title: Penang woodcarver keeps age-old craft alive as demand grows (VIDEO)
items.summary: The 63-year-old proprietor of Sung Dynasty Wood Carving learned the traditional craft from his late uncle, who had operated from Air Itam, before eventually taking over the trade. Labour of love Lee said he had initially resisted entering the labour-intensive trade when he was younger, choosing instead to work in other industries. Lee Chee Cheng showing the traditional Chinese name stamps that he also makes.

items.title: Experts urge holistic measures, warn teacher workload threatens mental health and classroom quality
items.summary: He said the pressure to achieve school performance targets often forces teachers to ‘steal’ breaks until late at night, thus affecting the quality of their personal and family lives. “Some teachers experience emotional stress, fear, and some even experience fatigue or burnout. Meanwhile, Mohammad Faiz said efforts to reduce teachers’ load must be accompanied by concrete and long-term measures, including expanding the appointment of teaching assistants based on school needs and increasing the recruitment of new teachers to fill vacancies.

items.title: Fadhlina hails Nadi Mahir school uniform instalment plan easing parents’ burden, empowering entrepreneurs
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 8 — The National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) Mahir initiative, enabling parents to purchase school uniforms on an instalment plan, is helping to ease their financial burden. Elaborating further, Fadhlina said various initiatives implemented through Nadi have directly benefited the community, including the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat, e-sports, skills training and entrepreneurship programmes. Over 42,000 students nationwide have joined the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat programme, with more than 73 from Nibong Tebal.

items.title: Chow stresses Penang Pakatan unity, BN exco retained as coalition eyes next GE
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 8 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) has decided to retain the Barisan Nasional (BN) state executive councillor in the state administration until the next general election (GE), said its chairman Chow Kon Yeow. He said the decision was reached at the Penang PH meeting today based on the electoral pact between PH and BN formed during the 2023 state election. The BN executive councillor is State Rural Development, Agrotechnology and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.

items.title: Seat swaps possible in Melaka, Zahid says negotiations must remain fair and principled
items.summary: KUDAT, Aug 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) remains open to negotiations on seat allocations for the Melaka State Election, including seat swaps, provided they are conducted honestly and in good faith, said BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The Deputy Prime Minister said the basic principle of the negotiations was that seats won by any party must be respected and should not simply be handed over to political partners. “As I have stated, the Melaka Chief Minister (Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh), who is also the Melaka BN chairman, said that as a matter of principle, in any negotiations, the position of any party that has won a seat must be respected.

items.title: Shrimp import talks with Thailand at final stage, resolution expected by mid‑August, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 8 — Discussions on the issue of shrimp imports from Thailand are at the final stage and are expected to be resolved by mid-August, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. The species are Penaeus esculentus (brown tiger shrimp), Fenneropenaeus merguiensis (banana shrimp), Penaeus vannamei (white shrimp), Penaeus monodon (tiger shrimp) and Penaeus stylirostris (blue shrimp). Mohamad said the Road to MAHA 2026 programme in Kota Bharu was the final instalment after similar programmes were held in Kedah, Selangor, Melaka and Labuan.

items.title: Perak Education Department vows fair handling of Chemor teacher bullying complaint, welfare prioritised
items.summary: Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said both parties should adopt a conciliatory approach in resolving the matter instead of blaming each other. “The matter has been brought to my attention, and we have asked the District Education Office and the Perak Education Department to investigate the allegations. Meanwhile, Perak Education director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said in a statement that the Perak Education Department (JPN) had taken note of the issue which went viral on social media.

items.title: Police seek owner, motive behind pink suitcase left at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS after explosive scare
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 8 — Police have opened an investigation paper to identify the owner and determine why a suitcase was left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex (ICQS), after a scan detected images resembling explosives and drugs. Kedah Police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said preliminary investigations found that the spot where the suitcase was left was outside CCTV coverage, making it difficult for police to identify the individual who left it there. Yesterday, police had carried out a process to neutralise a pink suitcase left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS.

items.title: Amirudin: Selangor govt to meet Panasonic workers over jobs, assistance after planned closure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 8 — The Selangor state government will meet workers expected to be affected by the closure of television production operations at Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PAVCKM) next week to discuss assistance and alternative employment opportunities. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting would be conducted by State Human Resources, Poverty Alleviation, Indigenous & Minority Affairs Committee chairman V. Papparaidu, together with representatives from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), to obtain relevant information from the affected workers. In a statement yesterday, Panasonic Malaysia Sdn Bhd (Panasonic) said production operations for two products would be closed, impacting 400 workers by the end of March next year.

items.title: AADK backs mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, cabin crew
items.summary: JERTIH, Aug 8 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) supports the move by Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) to make it compulsory for 1,260 Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilots to undergo drug screening following the recent arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia. AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move to tighten security controls and extend mandatory drug screening to all active pilots and cabin crew members was in line with the zero-tolerance policy towards drug abuse and trafficking. Ruslin said AADK had previously conducted drug abuse detection operations involving flight crew, including at MAS in April 2025 and AirAsia in December 2025.

items.title: Tabung Haji recovery plan addressed RM12.6b losses but further reforms needed, says RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) restructuring and recovery plan successfully restored the institution’s financial position after addressing RM12.6 billion in investment losses, while further reforms are needed to ensure its long-term sustainability, according to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The effectiveness of the recovery measures was reflected in TH’s improved financial performance, with investment income reaching RM4.64 billion last year, its highest since 2018. The commission concluded that the transfer preserved TH’s financial position and described the restructuring and recovery plan as instrumental in resolving the institution’s financial crisis.

items.title: Anwar pledges thorough probe into every Tabung Haji RCI finding following King’s decree
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The government has pledged to investigate every recommendation thoroughly and the findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. In a Facebook post today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was in line with the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring a comprehensive investigation into the report. “His Majesty’s order for a thorough investigation into the RCI report reflects the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring that every recommendation and finding is fully investigated without compromise,” he said.

items.title: MACC, police and IRB ramp up investigations into alleged Tabung Haji irregularities after RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Enforcement agencies have stepped up action following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution. By yesterday, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had remanded five individuals to assist in investigations into various alleged misconduct uncovered in the 211-page report released on July 29. Following severe asset impairment, the report recommended forensic audits into several high-risk investment decisions involving PT TH Indo Plantations, Emrail Sdn Bhd, Wellspring Worldwide Limited, Abraj Sdn Bhd, Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, TH Plantations Bhd, TH Properties Sdn Bhd, Alam Maritim Resources/TH Marine, TH Hotel & Residences Sdn Bhd and FGV Bhd, which allegedly resulted in substantial losses to depositors’ funds.
